_lisez-moi: Content shared by all audits. build_dossier.py and build_pptx.js merge it with audit.json: a key present in audit.json wins. categories: the grid (5 criteria per category). voies: the three to-do lanes (the first letter of a task code). priorites: P1 to P3, no dates.

outils.name: PageSpeed Insights, mobile
outils.releve: Performance, LCP, accessibility, best practices, SEO, agentic browsing
outils.role: Google's official tool for measuring the speed of a page. It loads the page like an average phone on a slow 4G connection, and gives a score out of 100, plus accessibility, best-practice and basic SEO scores. Google uses these same measurements to rank sites.

outils.name: PageSpeed Insights, desktop
outils.releve: Performance and real visitor data (Core Web Vitals over 28 days)
outils.role: The same Google tool, on desktop. It also shows real Chrome data: the speed actually experienced by the site's real visitors over the last 28 days, not just in a lab test.

outils.name: Security Headers
outils.releve: Grade, missing and present headers, server version displayed
outils.role: It checks the security instructions the server sends to the browser (the "headers"): force https, forbid unauthorised scripts, limit the information passed on. Graded from A+ to F. It is often the first test a security officer runs on a supplier's site.

outils.name: HTTP Observatory
outils.releve: Grade, score out of 100, tests passed
outils.role: The tool of the Mozilla foundation, which makes Firefox. It runs about ten security tests on the site and gives a grade from A+ to F and a score out of 100. It cross-checks Security Headers with a different method.

outils.name: SSL Server Test
outils.reglage: wait for the test to finish (2 to 3 min)
outils.releve: Grade, TLS version, certificate expiry date
outils.role: Qualys's tool, the world reference for testing the encryption of the connection between the visitor and the site (the https padlock): protocol version, certificate, known flaws. Graded from A+ to F.

outils.name: Internet.nl
outils.role: A Dutch public tool, backed by the government of the Netherlands. It checks that the site follows modern Internet standards: IPv6, domain name signing (DNSSEC), https and server security. Score as a percentage.

outils.name: Webbkoll
outils.releve: Third-party cookies, requests to other companies, CSP
outils.role: The tool of a Swedish privacy foundation. It opens the page like a visitor and lists the cookies and the data sent to other companies before any consent.

outils.name: Blacklight
outils.releve: Ad trackers, third-party cookies, session recording, fingerprinting
outils.role: The tool of the American investigative outlet The Markup. It simulates a visit and detects ad trackers, click tracking, session recording and browser fingerprinting.

outils.name: WAVE
outils.releve: AIM score, errors, contrast, images without a description
outils.role: WebAIM's tool (Utah State University), a reference for accessibility. It flags what hinders people with disabilities: images without a description, insufficient contrast, badly ordered headings. These defects hinder Google too.

outils.name: Nu HTML Checker
outils.role: The official validator of the W3C, the body that writes the web's standards. It reads the page code and lists the errors. Clean code is better read by browsers, by Google and by the AIs.

outils.name: LanguageTool
outils.reglage: lt.py script on the crawl's titles, descriptions, H1s and H2s
outils.role: A spelling and grammar checker. Run on all the titles, descriptions and headings collected by the crawl.

outils.name: "site:" search
outils.releve: Number of results, facts shown by Google (titles, descriptions)
outils.role: A Google search with the site: command shows the pages of the site that Google has kept, and how it presents them: titles, descriptions, snippets. It is exactly what a buyer sees.

outils.name: Brand search
outils.releve: Position of the site, description shown, language
outils.role: Microsoft's search engine. It also underpins Copilot and part of ChatGPT's searches: what it displays matters for the AIs.

outils.name: Share preview
outils.releve: Title, description and image shown when the page is shared (LinkedIn, Slack, X, WhatsApp)
outils.role: Shows the preview that social networks and messaging apps display when someone shares a page of the site. A preview with no image or description gets fewer clicks, and it is often a buyer's first impression.

outils.name: Rich results test
outils.role: Google's official tool that shows the structured information it finds in a page (organisation, software, article, FAQ). It is what lets Google display rich results and identify the publisher.

outils.name: Schema Markup Validator
outils.role: The validator of Schema.org, the vocabulary shared by Google, Bing and the AIs to describe a company, a product or an article. It reads all the structured data, even what Google does not display.

outils.name: Similarweb
outils.reglage: estimate: read it as a trend
outils.releve: Visits over 3 months, trend, countries, bounce
outils.role: A platform that estimates the audience of sites from panels of internet users, without access to our statistics. Useful for a trend, imprecise for a site of our size.

outils.name: Wikidata
outils.reglage: also search for the publisher's name
outils.role: The free database of the Wikimedia foundation (Wikipedia). Google and the AIs use it to identify a company: exact name, founding date, official site, executives.

outils.name: Backlink checker
outils.reglage: optional; an "I am human" box: the user must tick it, never Claude
outils.releve: Number of sites that link to the site, estimated authority, main links
outils.role: Counts the other sites that link to ours. These links are the site's reputation: Google and the AIs trust a site more when other reputable sites cite it.

assistants.name: ChatGPT
assistants.role: OpenAI's AI assistant, the most widely used. With web search on, it consults pages live, writes an answer and cites its sources.

assistants.name: Google AI Mode
assistants.role: The conversational mode of Google Search. It writes an answer from Google's results and shows the sites it relies on.

assistants.name: Brave
assistants.role: Brave's independent search engine, with its own index of pages. Its "Ask" feature writes a sourced answer.

assistants.name: Perplexity
assistants.condition: no account: only one question accepted, often behind a sign-up prompt (extract the text of the page)
assistants.role: An AI answer engine, widely used by technical profiles. It always cites its sources.

lexique: SEO
Natural search optimisation: everything that helps Google find, understand and rank the site well.
GEO
The same work for AI assistants (ChatGPT, Google AI Mode, Brave, Perplexity): being cited in their answers.
Indexing
A page being stored by Google so that it can appear in its results.
Page title (title)
The title shown in the browser tab and in blue in Google results. Not visible on the page itself.
Description (meta description)
The short text under the title in Google results. Without it, Google makes up the snippet.
H1, H2
The main heading of a page and its subheadings. Google uses them to understand the topic.
Glued words
Two words separated by a line break on screen but glued together for Google: "builtfor".
Alternative text (alt)
The description of an image, read by Google and by the screen readers of visually impaired people.
Sitemap
The list of pages you ask Google to read.
robots.txt
The file that tells robots what they are allowed to read.
301 / 302 redirect
The automatic forwarding of one address to another: 301 is permanent (Google transfers the reputation), 302 is temporary.
404 page
The "not found" page. A real 404 tells Google the page does not exist; redirecting to the home page misleads it.
Language tag (lang)
The indication, in the code, of the language of the page.
Canonical, hreflang
Hints for Google: which version of a page is the reference, and which are its translations.
Structured data (JSON-LD)
An identity card in machine language, hidden in the page: publisher name, address, date, software, author of an article.
llms.txt
A recent file, at the root of the site, that summarises the key facts for the AIs.
LCP
The time taken to display the main element of a page (often the large image). Google's target: under 2.5 s.
Core Web Vitals
Google's 3 measures of real visitors' experience: display speed, responsiveness, stability.
Security headers
Instructions the server sends to the browser (HSTS, CSP…) to block certain attacks.
Trackers, third-party cookies
Files and scripts from other companies (Google, LinkedIn…) that follow the visitor. The law requires their consent before loading them.
Search Console
Google's free tool that shows the clicks, the searches and the errors Google sees.
Wikidata
Wikipedia's free database, which Google and the AIs read to identify a company.
AI panel
The same 5 questions asked to the same AIs at each measurement, to track whether they cite us.
INP
Interaction to Next Paint: the time the page takes to react when you click or type. Good under 200 ms. It replaced FID in the Core Web Vitals.
CLS
Cumulative Layout Shift: how much the page "jumps" while loading. Good under 0.1.
TTFB
Time To First Byte: the time the server takes to send the first byte. Beyond 800 ms, everything else is late.
Server-side rendering (SSR)
The page arrives already written, instead of being built by JavaScript in the browser. Many AI robots do not run JavaScript: without server-side rendering, they see an empty page.
Compression (Brotli, gzip)
The server sends compressed pages: 3 to 5 times lighter, so faster.
Cache-Control
The header that tells the browser how long to keep an image or a script, so as not to download it again at every visit.
AI robots

Search crawlers decide citations: OAI-SearchBot (OpenAI), Claude-SearchBot (Anthropic), PerplexityBot. Training crawlers feed the models: GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended, CCBot. robots.txt can let each of them through or block it.
Open Graph
The tags that decide the title, description and image shown when a page is shared on LinkedIn or in a messaging app.
E-E-A-T
Experience, expertise, authoritativeness, trustworthiness: what Google looks for to trust a piece of content (named authors, sources, legal notices, reviews).
Backlinks
Links from other sites to ours. It is the site's reputation in the eyes of Google and the AIs.
WCAG
The international web accessibility rules: contrast, alternative texts, keyboard navigation, forms readable by a screen reader.
seo_geo: Natural search optimisation. The aim is for Google to understand the site, trust it and show it when a buyer looks for a solution like ours. It depends on technique (speed, settings), on text (titles, descriptions) and on reputation (the other sites that talk about us).

The same work for assistants such as ChatGPT, Google AI Mode, Brave or Perplexity. More and more buyers ask them directly "which solution should I choose?". The AIs mostly cite buying guides, comparisons, clear pages and the press.

regles: The same tools, at the same addresses, with the same settings
The same 5 questions to the AIs, asked 3 times each
PageSpeed run 3 times, keep the middle value
The same conditions: no account, cookies refused, same browser
Screenshots stored under the same number
bruit: PageSpeed: a gap of under 5 points means nothing; 10 points or more does
Security grades: any change counts, these tools are stable
AIs: a citation counts if it comes back at least 2 times out of 3
Similarweb: only a trend confirmed twice counts
remesure.promesse: What the team controls, and what can be promised: the fixes. What stays uncertain: positions in Google, traffic and citations by the AIs, which also depend on competitors and on what other sites write about us. No ranking promise.

voies: what you fix in the site's admin
Texts, figures, typos, titles, descriptions, images and their alternative texts, articles, pages, FAQ, external profiles (Wikidata, directories)
what you fix in the page code
Templates, semantic HTML, tags, structured data, responsive images, JavaScript and CSS, fonts, accessibility, forms, rendering without JavaScript
what you fix on the server
Redirects, HTTP codes, robots.txt, sitemap, security and cache headers, compression, CDN, certificate, response time, cookies and consent, Search Console access and measurement
priorites: stops Google or the AIs from reading the site, or damages trust
